//: THE SHARED MACHINE-TRANSPORT CONTRACT. Read tests/machine-transport/README.md before editing.
//contract: Each scenario is an argv a client wants to run on a MACHINE over SSH.
SSH has no argv API: a command is sent as ONE string the remote shell re-parses.
So every transport must compose that string identically, and every transport
must end up delivering the SAME argv to the remote process.
Two legs consume this file, and both must agree:
There is no Dart leg — see the README's "The Dart leg" section.
Adding a scenario means re-recording BOTH goldens (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1).
A scenario is never removed to make a leg pass.
//version: The contract revision. Bump on any change to `scenarios`; crates/shed-core/tests/machine_transport_contract.rs pins it so an edit here that forgets to re-record can't pass silently.
//C8: Version 3 (C8, plan 022 S6): `sx` was sunset, unreleased, in plan 016, and the RC hub it drove retired in S6 — every scenario that used to send `sx rc <verb>` argv was RE-POINTED, not deleted, onto the one composer that still calls `shed_core::machine::display_line` in production: shed-gx's discovery probe (`crates/shed-gx/src/discovery.rs::PROBE_SCRIPT`), invoked as `["sh", "-c", <script>]` by `shed_app::machine::exec`. Every quoting property the retired scenarios pinned survives, now carried as the `-c` script body instead of an `sx rc create --name <value>` flag value.

scenarios.why: the ordinary case: bare-safe tokens only — the shape gx's probe sends for its simplest possible script body

a bare-safe token (an absolute path, no metacharacters) must still be always-quoted — the property that distinguishes the house quoter from a conditional one. Retired: this used to be about `rc_bin` naming an absolute path when `sx` wasn't on the non-login SSH PATH; `rc_bin` is gone with `sx` (plan 016/022 S6), but the always-quote property still needs a bare-safe absolute-path value to pin
a bare command with flags and a path inside a script body — no escaping needed, but still delivered as one always-quoted argv element
a script body with a space — the most common non-trivial case a composed remote command carries
an empty argv element must survive as an explicit empty argument, not vanish
the quoter's own escape character; the classic off-by-one in hand-rolled quoting
must not be treated as a quoting character by either side
backslash is literal inside single quotes; a double-quoting transport would mangle it
must NOT be expanded by the outer shell composing the wire line — the whole point of quoting
an injection attempt via backticks and $() must reach the process as literal text
the injection case the always-quoter exists to close
a newline inside a quoted argument must survive as one argument, not split into two
internal whitespace must not re-split the argument
a value that looks like a flag must stay a value
non-ASCII must round-trip byte-for-byte through both transports
tilde expansion must NOT happen — a literal ~ is a legitimate value
a full realistic script, end to end — several hazards in one payload, the way a real probe script accumulates them (cf. gx-probe)
argv:
h=$HOME/.myagent
for f in "$h"/session-*.json; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  cat "$f"
done
echo 'done'

scenarios.why: shed-gx's discovery probe (plan 017): a whole multi-line POSIX sh script as ONE argv element - newlines, $-expansions, a command substitution and a backslash-semicolon. It is the string the gx lane's credential seam sends over the reach, so a transport that mangles it reads no discovery record at all.
argv:
h=${GROK_HOME:-$HOME/.grok}
for f in "$h"/gx-remote*.json; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  cat "$f" 2>/dev/null
  printf "\n---\n"
done
printf "===token===\n"
t="$h/gx-remote.token"
find "$t" -prune -type f -perm 0600 -user "$(id -un)" -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null
exit 0
